Summary: Discernment is the Spirit-shaped ability to distinguish truth from error and good from merely plausible. It grows through Scripture, prayer, community, and experience, and it is needed most where falsehood wears a disguise — in teaching, in guidance, and in cultural pressures. Discernment is humble: it tests everything, holds fast to what is good, and admits it can be wrong.
RelatedPeople: King Solomon; Paul; John the Apostle
